Part 2&3 地点 PLACE

Describe a city that you think is very interesting/famous

描述一个你觉得非常有趣/出名的城市

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a city that you think is very interesting/famous

  • Where it is (它在哪里)
  • What it is famous for (它因什么出名)
  • How you knew this city (你是怎么知道这座城市的)
  • And explain why you think it is very interesting/famous (并解释为什么你觉得它非常有趣/出名)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a city that you think is very interesting/famous

The city I'd like to talk about is Shenzhen, which sits right on the southern coast of China, next to Hong Kong. It was a small fishing village just over forty years ago, but now it's one of the country's most prosperous and fastest-growing metropolises. I first heard about Shenzhen from the news and from my parents, because it's often described as a symbol of China's reform and opening up. Later, when I started paying attention to technology, I realised that many of the tech companies I use every day, like Tencent and DJI, are based there. What Shenzhen is most famous for is being a tech hub and a special economic zone. Places like Qianhai are packed with skyscrapers and startups, and the whole city seems to be designed around innovation and business. The average age there is quite young, which gives the streets a really energetic, bustling atmosphere. The reason I find it so interesting is the contrast between its past and its present. I mean, the idea that a fishing village could transform into a world-class city within one generation is almost unbelievable, and it says a lot about how fast China has changed. I think Shenzhen is a place where you can literally see the future being built, and that's why it fascinates me so much.

深圳，位于中国南部沿海、紧邻香港。四十多年前还是小渔村，如今是最繁华、发展最快的都市之一。从新闻和父母那里听说它，它是改革开放的象征；后来关注科技，发现腾讯、大疆等公司都在这里。它因科技中心和特区出名，前海满是摩天大楼和创业公司，城市年轻、街道热闹。有趣之处在于过去与现在的反差：一代人从渔村变成世界级城市，仿佛能看到未来正在被建造。

Q2What advantages can tourism bring to a city?

I think tourism can bring quite a lot of benefits to a city. For one thing, it creates jobs in hotels, restaurants and transport, which is important for local employment. It also brings in money from outside, so the government can spend more on roads and public facilities. On top of that, tourism builds a better reputation, because visitors spread the word about what they've seen. Having said that, these benefits only appear when tourism is managed properly.

旅游带来就业（酒店、餐饮、交通）、外部资金（政府可投入公共设施）、提升城市声誉。但前提是管理得当。

Q3Why do some young people like to live in cities?

Well, there are a few main reasons. Firstly, cities offer far more job opportunities, especially in tech and finance, which young people find attractive. Secondly, the lifestyle suits them better. I mean, there are countless cafes, gyms and events, so it's easier to make friends and have fun. Another factor is convenience, since everything is close by. City life does come with high rents and stress, but for most young people, the chance of a better future outweighs those drawbacks.

工作机会多（科技、金融）、生活方式丰富（咖啡馆、健身房、活动）、生活便利。虽有高房租和压力，但年轻人认为发展机会更重要。

Q4Do most elderly people live in the city or in the countryside?

In China, I'd say the majority of elderly people live in the countryside, because many of them grew up there and feel more at home among familiar neighbours. However, a growing number are moving to cities, especially when their children settle there and need help with childcare, so the picture is changing. Generally speaking, though, I think the countryside is still where most older people spend their retirement, because the pace of life is slower and the air is cleaner.

多数老人住在农村（熟悉的环境、邻里），但越来越多老人搬去城市帮子女带孩子。总体而言农村仍是多数老人养老之地，节奏慢、空气好。

Q5Do you think well-developed tourism will have negative effects on local people?

To be honest, I think it can, even though tourism is generally positive. When a city becomes too popular, housing prices and the cost of daily goods tend to rise, which makes life harder for residents. Crowded streets and attractions can also be stressful for nearby residents. That said, whether the effect is negative depends on how the city manages it. If the government controls the number of visitors and protects public spaces, the downsides can be kept under control.

过度旅游会推高房价和物价、让居民生活更累。但影响好坏取决于管理：若政府控制游客数量、保护公共空间，负面影响可控。

Q6What are the benefits of urbanization?

Urbanization brings several clear benefits. For a start, it concentrates resources, so hospitals, schools and transport networks can serve far more people efficiently. It also creates a stronger economy, because businesses can share workers, suppliers and ideas in one place. In addition, city life tends to offer more chances for education and self-improvement, which is why so many young people move there. Of course, rapid urbanization needs to be planned carefully, otherwise it can lead to housing problems and pollution.

城市化集中资源（医院、学校、交通效率更高）、促进经济（共享人才与供应链）、提供更多教育机会。但需合理规划，否则引发住房和污染问题。

Q7Do you think the big cities in China today will become even larger in the future?

I imagine some of them will keep growing, though not as quickly as before. On the one hand, big cities still attract young people with better jobs, so the population will likely keep rising for a while. On the other hand, the government has been encouraging development in smaller cities, and remote working makes it possible to live elsewhere, which could slow the growth. The largest cities might expand further, but medium-sized cities will see the most growth.

大城市短期内仍会增长（吸引年轻人），但政府鼓励中小城市发展、远程办公普及会减缓增速。未来超大城继续扩张，但增长主力可能是中型城市。
